name: Human Catapult
description: A catapult that launches the VR PLAYER. Walk into the player-sized basket, set the ANGLE and FORCE on the console, then hit FIRE — the arm swings and the player's body is given a ballistic launch velocity, arcing up and away under gravity. A live launch-velocity arrow and predicted parabola preview where you'll land. Sibling of the teaching `catapult` (which throws a ball); here YOU are the projectile, so the trajectory is felt, not watched. Uses the proven jump_pad / XRToolsPlayerBody.velocity player-launch pattern.
theoreticalGrounding: The surest way to understand a launch vector is to be the projectile. p(t)=p0+v0*t+0.5*g*t^2 — angle and force set v0; gravity owns you the instant you leave the cup.

dna.default: foresight=parabola, vectors=velocity - together these are the shipped machine exactly: the full predicted parabola drawn from the basket, plus ONE accent-coloured launch-velocity arrow, with gravity left undrawn. `parabola` is the fall-through arm of _foresight_mesh and runs _arc_mesh, which is the shipped p(t)=p0+v0*t+0.5*g*t^2 loop character for character - same 0.08 s sampling, same `while t < 4.0`, same break at p.y<0, same SurfaceTool LINE_STRIP. `velocity` is the fall-through arm of _build_indicators and runs the same two lines that always built the single arrow, in the same order, so _accent_mats gets the same one entry. MEASURED, not assumed: all three placements carry the bare token form - `human_catapult` in ForcesArena, `human_catapult:90:0` in Force_Preview and VFM_05_Launch. That form is artifact:rotation:y_offset, not config, so not one of them passes a foresight or vectors key, and the new apply_grid_config returns without rebuilding unless a key is present AND differs from the value the node already holds.
dna.was: a machine whose only knobs were MAGNITUDES - launch_force, launch_angle, gravity_magnitude. Turning them flings the same body further; none of them is an argument. And the flight is an EVENT, which one still cannot hold. Worse, apply_grid_config was actively harmful: it queue_free()d every child and call_deferred("_ready") on ANY call, including one whose dictionary named nothing this machine owns - and because queue_free only detaches at end of frame, the deferred rebuild could run while the old frame was still parented. That is the force_pad trap, and it is fixed here in the same way.
dna.shares_vocabulary_with: catapult and force_pad, both words and both value lists character for character. The three are one machine at three scales - each hands a body a velocity and lets gravity have it back - and only the DEFAULT differs, honestly, because they shipped at different rungs of the same ladder: catapult was born drawing the whole parabola AND the gravity arrow (parabola/sum), force_pad was born drawing none of the arc and one arrow (none/velocity), and this one was born in between, whole arc and one arrow. Three siblings measuring alike on the same question is what makes the shared word honest rather than decorative.
dna.why_the_word_fits_here: launch_arc refused foresight last pass on the correct ground that its parabola is a strobe of a flight already completed, so nothing is being foreseen. This machine has a FIRE button, a basket you stand in, and an arc drawn from that basket BEFORE the button is pressed - the word's literal condition. And because the payload is the PLAYER, the axis stops being a display option and becomes a question about consent: at `none` you climb into a cup and find out where you land; at `landing` the floor already says; at `parabola` the whole flight is written before you move.
dna.still_note: both axes are static geometry resolved at build time - no rate, no decay, no animation. _process only calls _refresh() while _firing, and the armed emission pulse needs a player body in the Area3D, so with no player present the frame is deterministic and one still is a complete account. Note for the sweep: at the shipped angle/force the arc runs about 15 m from a 3.2 m frame, so the union camera is set by the arc; three of the four foresight values reach 7-15 m and only `none` is small in that frame. The pairwise difference is a 15 m emissive line present or absent, so the risk here is a large bite, not a null.
dna.declines: launch_force, launch_angle and gravity_magnitude stay plain numeric exports reachable through apply_grid_config but undeclared as axes - a longer arrow and a further arc are size changes, not different claims. Also declined: an axis on the arm swing or the rest pitch, which is animation and invisible to a still.

human_catapult.name: Human Catapult
human_catapult.description: Heavy timber frame + throwing arm + a player-sized basket (StaticBody floor you stand on, low walls, harness). An Area3D (player_body layer) arms the seat when you step in; ANGLE/FORCE sliders + a FIRE button launch you. Live velocity arrow + parabola preview. DNA: launch_force, launch_angle, gravity_magnitude.
human_catapult.qfep_connection: F_force: launch velocity + gravity = the arc you fly; the player becomes the projectile.
